samples.summary: Clearing a boolean key can make an image run byte-identical to an adjacent identical image run, and `normalizeInlines` (unlike the paste path) merges structural inlines — losing one image
samples.evidence: `normalizeInlines` (block-helpers.ts:76-86) merges any two adjacent runs for which `inlineStylesEqual` is true, with **no** `isStructuralInline` guard. `inlineStylesEqual` compares images through `imageDataEqual` (types.ts:383-398), i.e. two *identical* images (copy/paste an image beside itself) compare equal — exactly the case types.ts:432-436 and TextEditor.normalizeInlineList (view/text-editor.ts:3722, issue #726) say must never merge. Before this change a toggle-off wrote `bold: false` onto the styled image run, which differed from its unstyled twin and kept them split; now `styleOffAsClear` (document.ts:399-418) rewrites it to `undefined` and `mergeInlineStyle` (block-helpers.ts:316-325) *deletes* the key, so run A's style becomes exactly `{image}` — equal to twin B. `applyInlineStyle` ends with `normalizeInlines(newInlines)` (line 380), which concatenates them into one 2-character run under a single `style.image`: the second image is dropped from the model while the offsets still count both characters (layout emits one image segment for the 2-char inline). Repro: two adjacent identical images, image A bolded, B not; select only A and press Cmd+B (summary reads bold-on for that run, so the toggle sends `bold:false`).

samples.summary: Clearing `underline`/`strikethrough` leaves their dependent keys (`underlineStyle`, `underlineColor`, `strikeStyle`) behind, so the run still cannot re-merge and a later re-apply resurrects the old variant
samples.evidence: `BOOLEAN_INLINE_STYLE_KEYS` covers only the six flags. `underlineStyle`/`underlineColor` are documented as "meaningful only when `underline` is set" (types.ts:151-157) and `strikeStyle` likewise (types.ts:159-164), and `inlineStylesEqual` compares all three (types.ts:409-412). So toggling underline off on a run that carries `underlineStyle:'double'` clears only `underline`; the run keeps a dead `underlineStyle` and can never re-merge with the neighbour it was split from — the exact invariant the change claims to restore — and re-applying underline later silently comes back double/coloured. The Yorkie path has the same hole: `removedInlineStyleAttrs` is only fed the patch, so only the `underline` attribute is removed from the Tree (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1883).

samples.summary: In the collaborative store the cleared run is not re-merged in the CRDT, so the cached document (one run) and the Tree (three runs) diverge and the #749 split persists after any re-read
samples.evidence: `applyStyle` updates the cache with `applyInlineStyleHelper` (line 1707), which now runs `normalizeInlines` and collapses the three split runs back to one. `applyStyleInTree` only styles/removes attributes on the existing inline nodes and deletes *empty* ones (lines 1884-1904) — it never merges adjacent equal-attribute inline nodes, and `treeNodeToBlock` (line 418-434) performs no normalization when re-parsing. So after a toggle-off the cache reports 1 inline while the Tree still holds 3, and any re-read (remote patch, `dirty`) resurrects 3 runs. Benign visually, but it means the fix's central claim ("the run stayed split forever") is not actually fixed for the production store, and it widens an existing cache/Tree structural divergence that other code samples by inline index (e.g. line 1570-1571 resolves an inline index against the cache).

samples.summary: `styleOffAsClear` calls the linear-scan `findBlock` once per visited block slice, making a toggle-off over a large selection or table quadratic
samples.evidence: `findBlock` (document.ts:176-186) scans `_document.blocks`, then header/footer, then `findBlockInCells`, whose fallback is a full recursive walk of every table in body+header+footer (lines 214-220) whenever the layout-time parent map lacks the id. `styleOffAsClear` is invoked from inside the `visitRangeSlices` / `visitCellRectangleSlices` visitors (lines 377 and 431), i.e. once per block slice, so a select-all Cmd+B-off over an N-block document does N linear scans (O(N^2)), and a cell-rectangle toggle over a large table does one per cell block. The block is only needed for its named style, which is constant per block — resolving it once per unique block (or memoizing) avoids this. On the "hottest editing path" the comment itself cites, this is a user-visible stall risk.

samples.summary: The new false→undefined normalization sits only in `Doc.applyInlineStyle`/`applyInlineStyleToCells`; the batched `docStore.applyStyles` path writes styles straight to the store, so a boolean patch routed there would still store a dead `false`
samples.evidence: `stepSelectionFontSizeImpl` calls `docStore.applyStyles(...)` directly (editor.ts:1095-1102), bypassing `Doc` entirely, and `MemDocStore.applyStyles` (store/memory.ts:222) / `YorkieDocStore.applyStyles` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1733-1775) pass the caller's style through unchanged. Today only `{ fontSize }` goes through it, so nothing is broken now, but the invariant "no stored boolean `false`" is enforced in one of the two write paths only; the batch path (which the store doc comment at store/store.ts:82-89 actively recommends for multi-range single-undo writes) is an unguarded route to the state the change exists to eliminate.
searchedFor: grep for boolean false in src

verdict.reason: All claimed code is present exactly as described and the path is reachable. `normalizeInlines` (block-helpers.ts:76-86) merges adjacent runs on `inlineStylesEqual` alone, with no `isStructuralInline` guard; `inlineStylesEqual` (types.ts:404-424) routes images through `imageDataEqual` (types.ts:383-399), which is pure value equality, so two identical adjacent images compare equal. The repo itself documents that equality is NOT the right test for structural inlines (types.ts:426-440) and the sibling normalizer text-editor.ts:3712-3730 does carry the `!isStructuralInline(...)` guard (#726) — block-helpers.ts:81 and document.ts:912 do not. `styleOffAsClear` (document.ts:399-418, boolean keys at document.ts:39-46) turns a toggle-off `bold:false` into `undefined`, and `mergeInlineStyle` (block-helpers.ts:316-325) deletes the key, so the styled image run's style collapses to exactly `{image}` and becomes equal to its unstyled twin. `applyInlineStyle` then calls `normalizeInlines(newInlines)` at block-helpers.ts:380, concatenating the two image runs into one 2-char run under a single `style.image` — the second image is dropped while offsets still count both characters. The write path is live: Document.applyInlineStyle (document.ts:375-380) -> store.applyStyle -> MemoryStore.applyStyle (memory.ts:213-215) -> applyInlineStyleHelper. No guard anywhere on that path filters structural inlines, so `already-guarded` does not apply; nothing is misquoted, so `not-present` does not apply; and image loss + a broken offset/model invariant is data loss, which is critical under the correctness rubric, so `out-of-scope` does not apply.

mergedFrom.summary: Every B/I/U/S toggle-off now emits a `removeStyleByPath` op instead of a `styleByPath` set; concurrent-edit resolution between remove-attribute and set-attribute ops is not the same LWW path the old `bold=false` write used

finding.summary: Every style write, including the now-hot pure-clear toggle-off, re-asserts the node's full existing attribute map, which can clobber a concurrent remote attribute change
finding.evidence: `tree.styleByPath([...blockPath, i], { ...existingAttrs, ...styleAttrs })` re-sends every attribute already on the node even when `styleAttrs` is empty (the pure-clear case `{bold: undefined}` that, per the comment added at lines 1873-1875, is now every B/I/U/S toggle-off). The comment two lines above states styleByPath 'only merges', so passing `existingAttrs` is unnecessary; because it is sent with a fresh local timestamp, an LWW-per-attribute Tree resolves it over a concurrent peer's change to an unrelated attribute (e.g. peer sets `color` while this client toggles bold off), reverting the peer's edit. The delta puts this redundant full-attribute rewrite on the hottest editing path.

verdict.reason: The code exists as quoted. `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:1885-1889` reads `const existingAttrs = inlines[i].attributes ?? {}` and calls `tree.styleByPath([...blockPath, i], { ...existingAttrs, ...styleAttrs })`, followed by `removeStyleByPath` for cleared keys. The comment immediately above (lines 1871-1875) itself states "styleByPath only merges", so re-sending the node's whole existing attribute map is redundant — and for the pure-clear case (`{bold: undefined}`), `serializeInlineStyle` drops the key (see `setIfDefined` usage at lines 106-133 and `removedInlineStyleAttrs` at 144-163), leaving `styleAttrs` empty so the write consists solely of stale re-assertions. Because each `styleByPath` op carries a fresh local timestamp and Yorkie Tree attributes are per-attribute LWW, a re-asserted stale value can win over a concurrent remote change to an unrelated attribute (e.g. a peer setting `color` while this client toggles bold off), reverting the peer's edit — a data-overwrite/lost-update path squarely in the correctness lane, and per the surrounding comments and the test at packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:209-228 this is now the hottest B/I/U/S toggle path. Note the sibling block-style write at line 1418 passes only the intended `attrs` (no existing-attribute re-assertion) plus `removeStyleByPath` at 1424, confirming the full-map merge is not required for correct clearing. I found no caller-side guard, no equality short-circuit before the call, and the Yorkie SDK is not vendored in this tree, so I cannot demonstrate the write is a no-op at the CRDT layer; nothing supports a refutation ground.

finding.summary: Yorkie tree write ignores the superscript/subscript mutual exclusion that the cache write applies, so the CRDT keeps both flags while the local cache shows one
finding.evidence: `applyStyle` (line 1707) updates the cache with `applyInlineStyleHelper(block, from, to, style)`, and that helper (packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:337-343) resolves `{superscript:true}` into `{superscript:true, subscript:undefined}` and, via `mergeInlineStyle` (block-helpers.ts:316-325), *deletes* `subscript` from the run. The tree path (`applyStyleInTree`, line 1716) is handed the RAW `style`: `serializeInlineStyle(style)` at line 1882 emits only `superscript:'true'` and `removedInlineStyleAttrs(style)` at line 1883 returns `[]` because `subscript` is not a key of the patch. Since `styleByPath` only merges, the pre-existing `subscript='true'` attribute survives on the Tree node. Ctrl+. on subscripted text (text-editor.ts:899) therefore leaves the CRDT with both `superscript` and `subscript` set; `parseInlineStyle` (line 168-173) reads both back on reload or on any remote-driven cache invalidation, so the run silently changes appearance/state relative to what the user saw. This is exactly the 'styleByPath cannot delete' class of bug the surrounding comment block (lines 1871-1881) claims is handled on this path.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: `applyStyle` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1707) updates the cache via `applyInlineStyleHelper`, whose implementation (block-helpers.ts:337-343 + mergeInlineStyle 316-325) enforces superscript/subscript mutual exclusion by resolving the opposite key to `undefined` and deleting it from the run. But line 1716 hands the RAW `style` to `applyStyleInTree` (same at 1760 in `applyStyles`). Inside `applyStyleInTree`, `serializeInlineStyle(style)` (line 1882) emits only the keys present in the patch (setIfDefined, lines 112-113) and `removedInlineStyleAttrs(style)` (line 1883) returns names only for keys present-and-undefined (line 147 `if (key in style && style[key] === undefined)`), so for a `{superscript:true}` patch it returns `[]`. `styleByPath` at line 1886 merges only, so a pre-existing `subscript='true'` attribute survives on the Tree node — exactly the hazard the comment at 1871-1881 documents. The path is unguarded end-to-end: text-editor.ts:899 calls `toggleStyle({superscript:true})`, `toggleStyle` (2858-2903) iterates only `Object.keys(style)` and never adds the opposite key, and document.ts:375-377 `applyInlineStyle`/`styleOffAsClear` (399-418) only rewrites keys already `false`. `parseInlineStyle` (172-173) reads both flags back on reload or cache rebuild; downstream `paint-layout.ts:378-382`, `layout.ts:118` and `export/docx-style-map.ts:79-80` (emits two conflicting w:vertAlign) see both set, and a later toggle-off of superscript leaves the stale subscript active. Real CRDT/cache divergence and broken invariant — correctness lane, major.
